stem: The polynomial $p(w)=w^3+aw^2+bw+5$, where $a,b\in\mathbb R$, has a root $2+i$.

parts.label: a

title: An Apollonius circle and a nearest point
stem: A complex number $z=x+iy$ satisfies $|z-2|=2|z+1|$. The points $-1$, $2$ and $P=3+4i$ are shown.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Show that the locus is a circle, and state its centre and radius.

parts.label: b

title: A conditional committee choice
stem: A committee of five is chosen uniformly from six girls and five boys. Two of the girls are school captains.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the number of committees containing exactly three girls.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Given that the committee has exactly three girls, find the probability that at least one captain is chosen.

steps.text: Choose the girls and boys separately: $\binom63\binom52$.
Each unordered committee is counted exactly once.
Use the complement: $\binom43/\binom63=4/20$ contains no captain.
Conditioning fixes the number of girls; the boy choices cancel from the ratio.

title: A weighted geometric sum proved by induction
stem: Let $T_n=\sum_{r=1}^n r2^r$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Prove by induction that $T_n=(n-1)2^{n+1}+2$ for all positive integers n.

parts.label: b

title: A parameter changes solvability
stem: The system is $x+y+z=3$, $x+2y+3z=6$, $2x+3y+(k+4)z=10$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Determine the values of k for which the system has no solution or a unique solution.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: For the unique-solution case, express x, y and z in terms of k.

steps.text: Subtract the sum of the first two equations from the third.
$k=0$ gives a contradiction, so there is no solution. For $k\ne0$, z is fixed and then x,y are uniquely fixed.
The second minus the first gives $y+2z=3$.

answerSummary: $k=0$ gives a contradiction, so there is no solution. For $k\ne0$, z is fixed and then x,y are uniquely fixed. $(x,y,z)=(1/k,\ 3-2/k,\ 1/k)$.

title: Divisibility and the parity of a quotient
stem: For positive integers n, define $b_n=(7^n-1)/6$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Prove by induction that b_n is an integer.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Determine exactly when b_n is odd, giving a proof.

steps.text: $b_{k+1}=7b_k+1$, an integer if $b_k$ is an integer.
Induction establishes integrality for every positive n.
Every term is odd, so the parity of the sum is the parity of the number of terms.
b_n is odd exactly when n is odd.
